spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the spec's encapsulateKey()/decapsulateKey() one-step derivation of an AES-GCM CryptoKey from an ML-KEM-768 public key — the exact five-argument shape from the WICG draft — then proves byte-identity by raw export and completes an AES-GCM round-trip.

interactive.rationale: An editable message, run/reset buttons, and a five-step stage that activates progressively with real hex artifacts and the decrypted plaintext.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises encapsulateKey() deriving a session key with no manual derivation step and that key immediately encrypting a message; the page delivers the full end-to-end pattern.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported browsers get the honest flag note and warn status, run failures surface the real exception, the key-identity check and round-trip check are asserted separately, and the decrypted output is HTML-escaped before innerHTML insertion.

references.rationale: Sibling links only — no https://chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 link on the page (shared gap across the five webcrypto concepts).

conformance.rationale: The suite's encapsulateKey/decapsulateKey typeof assertions are exactly this page's dependency; failures in this unflagged Chromium 141 session are the expected absent WebCryptoPQC surface.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CLI/CDP (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): initial DOM shows the visible flag note, warn status, and all five steps in the dimmed pending state; zero console errors, no unintended failed requests; the run flow could not be driven interactively here.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts unsupported runs, the combined key-identity + round-trip outcome, and run failures with error names.

design_system.rationale: Tokenised colours, but the default-visible warn status (--accent-amber on --bg-stone) computes ~3.5:1, under the AA 4.5:1 bar for its 0.8rem bold size; also note .step.pending relies on opacity 0.55, dimming its text below AA while pending (acceptable as disabled-state styling but worth a look).

accessibility.rationale: Labelled textarea, native buttons, role=status aria-live status line, and step progression conveyed through text content changes rather than colour alone; pending steps are informational placeholders.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3 measures 0px horizontal overflow with word-break on step details; desktop 1280×800 clean; only the environmental Google Fonts request fails.

openQuestions.title: Add the chromestatus feature link to this page's see-also
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires the chromestatus.com/feature/5198951632470016 self-heal link on every page; this concept links siblings only. One-line additive fix shared across the webcrypto set.

openQuestions.title: Fix the sub-AA warn status contrast and review pending-step dimming
openQuestions.detail: status-line.warn (--accent-amber on --bg-stone, ~3.5:1 at 0.8rem bold) is the default visible state in unflagged browsers and misses AA 4.5:1; .step.pending's opacity 0.55 drops charcoal step text to roughly 4:1 as well. Darker amber plus a less transparent pending treatment (or explicit muted colour tokens) would clear the bar.

openQuestions.title: Capture the five-step flagged success run as evidence
openQuestions.detail: The progressive stage activation, KEM ciphertext sizes, AES-GCM key identity check, and decrypted round-trip could not be observed in this unflagged Chromium 141. Run once in a WebCryptoPQC-enabled Chrome 150+ and record the completed stage.

summary: The strongest teaching page of the set: a real end-to-end hybrid encryption pattern using encapsulateKey()/decapsulateKey() straight into AES-GCM, with byte-identity proof, XSS-safe output, and an honest unsupported fallback. Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CLI/CDP (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): honest warn state, clean console, no unintended failed requests, no overflow on either class. Open items: chromestatus link, warn/pending contrast, and flagged-run evidence.
